notes.title: Update 6/5/2024
notes.content:
[h1]Changes for 6/5/2024[/h1]
Main game:
[list]
[*]Externalized backpack headset badge system.
[/list]

[h1]What does this mean?[/h1]
It means that I am managing the badge textures externally now, which means any time a headset is connected to climbey it will show up on my end and I can upload a custom badge texture for it without updating the main build of the game to include it as a texture.
This is much more future proof than before and will allow me to keep up with any new headsets coming out on the fly!
It's a fairly inconsequential update for the most part, just a neat little system I've been wanting to put in for a while now that will guarantee people's headset badges reflect their actual headsets used in multiplayer.

[h1]What have you been doing??[/h1]
I've still been focusing hard on Facepunch's S&box and building games inside it, with the recent news of PSVR2 getting a PC adapter I see very little need for Climbey to go through the extreme hassle that is publishing on PS5.

This is probably the last Climbey update you'll get for a while, unless I suddenly get another jolt of inspiration and feel like adding more stuff to it!

-Shadowbrain

notes.title: Update 1/10/2022
notes.content:
Main game:
[list]
[*]Swapped default and joystick-walk-optimized SteamVR input mappings.
[/list]

This is so less people complain about rotation being on both joysticks, despite them just being able to swap the inputs themselves before this.

I think people just don't generally know about SteamVR input or something because this has been a recurring thing for months :p

The default expected mapping for Climbey used to be rotation on both joysticks, grip and controller moving for walking.
People generally expect joystick walking for some reason despite it being a lot less comfortable and nice, so I've swapped the input mapping so rotation is only on the left hand and walking is on the right, which I already made a default choice for in the SteamVR Input binding screen years ago.

The Oculus jump tweak was a result of me going over some older code and noticing that that was still active on all devices with Oculus in their tracking system name, now it specifically checks for the Rift CV1. 
Hopefully this will end up making jumps feel more accurate on other Oculus headsets, or you might not notice anything at all, we'll see.

notes.title: Update 3/31/2019 - Finally back to stable branch!
notes.content:
This is a rather large update, it's what I've been holding on to on the beta branch for way too long so it's long overdue!

Demo:
[list]
[*]Updated demo build to reflect the current state of the game and gameplay better, also updating to include the finger tracking support via SteamVR finger tracking API
[/list]

Main game:
[list]
[*]Tweaked jump controller release timing, should make jumps more predictable and consistent.
[*]Removed snow- it’s Spring now! This will also make snowballs disabled by default instead of being enabled by default. You can still turn them on if you want though.
[*]Fixed “controller visible” not working as intended for non-Vive or Oculus controllers.
[*]Fixed all the comfort option buttons randomly working/not working.
[*]Fixed “babyjump” ledge jump related glitch
[*]Fixed retry bug that allowed you to fling across the map on retry.
[*]Upgraded Unity project from 2018.1.0f6 to 2018.3.10f1. This updates the physics engine which should bring performance improvements in some levels with a lot of moving platforms, for example.
[*]Upgraded SteamVR plugin.
[*]Made finger tracking future proof by making it use the SteamVR API for finger curls.
[*]Made “skip level” button a press and hold button.
[*]Added automatic re-check for knuckles controllers/finger tracking.
[*]Added “load levels” button to the workshop level list for people with a lot of Workshop content to prevent hangs when initially spawning.
[*]Added “load upvoted levels” which is a filter for the level list that needs to be built up but persists throughout your playthrough.
[*]Added Pimax badge for multiplayer.
[*]Added a check for duplicate names so they get (#) added to their name in multiplayer.
[*]Added crown buttons next to player names so the host of the room can transfer ownership of the room over if they’re leaving or going AFK, reducing the risk of having an AFK host.
[*]Added Performance Settings window to multiplayer lobby room.
[*]Reworked foot tracking implementation.
[*]Maybe fixed Mixed Reality view for streamers, using the “camera” tracker role and assigning its pose to the main pose should make it work.
[/list]

Level Editor:
[list]
[*]Added a delay to the picture taking mode in the level editor to prevent accidental thumbnail pictures from being taken.
[*]Level editor’s picture taking now needs both triggers to be pressed to take a picture. Hopefully these two fixes make it so there’s less black thumbnails on the workshop.
[/list]

notes.title: Beta branch notice
notes.content:
Hey folks! 
Sorry for going dark there for a bit, I've been hard at work with crushing bugs from upgrading Climbey's game engine and it seems like there's never an end to the bugs I'm running in to, so I figured I'd put up a new public beta branch!

Again, to get into a game's beta branch just hit right click on the game in your steam library, go to properties, then hit the beta tab and select it from the dropdown.

I recommend Knuckles users switch to this beta as it makes the finger tracking work a lot more consistently.

Main game:
[list]
[*]Upgraded Unity project from 2018.1.0f6 to 2018.3.5f1. This updates the physics engine which should bring performance improvements in some levels with a lot of moving platforms, for example.
[*]Tweaked jump controller release timing, should make jumps more predictable and consistent.
[*]Fixed retry bug that allowed you to fling across the map on retry.
[*]Upgraded SteamVR plugin.
[*]Reworked foot tracking implementation.
[*]Made finger tracking future proof by making it use the SteamVR API for finger curls.
[*]Added an ownership transfer button to everyone's names if you are the host on a server, which will allow you to transfer ownership to a specific person before you leave the server.
[*]Added a check for duplicate names so they get (#) added to their name.
[*]Made "forward" rendering mode turn off lights in levels to prevent flickering.
[/list]

Level Editor:
[list]
[*]Added a delay to the picture taking mode in the level editor to prevent accidental thumbnail pictures from being taken.
[*]Level editor’s picture taking now needs both triggers to be pressed to take a picture.
[/list]

The beta is currently quite stable but there's just a few quirks I'm not comfortable with.

Known issues:
[list]
[*]The frame rate drops dramatically if you don't have the game window focused on your desktop. This seems to be a Unity bug and I'm not sure I can even fix it without just upgrading the engine again.
[*]Feet left/right assignment sometimes doesn't match I think? Not entirely sure on this one.
[*]The game will start with cameras in your hands sometimes, this mainly happens when you have the SteamVR overlay open as the game starts/loads, I recommend just hitting the "Start" button in the menu since it starts off open, assuming you can reach it, this should reload things and make your input work fine.
[/list]

If you find any more issues do let me know!

Note: The new foot tracking requires people to set their left/right foot up properly in the tracker role assignments. Please make sure it’s set up right before starting the game.

notes.title: Update 7/2/2017
notes.content:
Main game:
[list]
[*]Added “-releasesensitivity <number>” as a launch option. The number has to be between 0 and 1, setting it to 0 makes it reset to the default value (0.0075 for Vive, 0.0008 for Touch).
Making this customizable allows people to fine tune their play if they want to, or fix triggers that prematurely release as one of my controllers does.
[*]Added initial support for Valve Knuckles controllers (blindly, don’t have my hardware in yet), I will keep tweaking this for a little while to see if I can make it play as nicely as regular controller triggers do, if not better.
[/list]

The default release number for Touch is so much smaller because the spring on Touch controller triggers is much weaker than the Vive's trigger spring.

The release value is basically how far the trigger needs to move back up for your hand to release the thing it's holding.

(Knuckles controllers also respond to the release sensitivity, their default is 0.01)

[*]Added “-releasesensitivity <number>” as a launch option. The number has to be between 0 and 1, setting it to 0 makes it reset to the default value (0.0075 for Vive, 0.0008 for Touch).
Making this customizable allows people to fine tune their play if they want to, or fix triggers that prematurely release as one of my controllers does.
[*]Added initial support for Valve Knuckles controllers (blindly, don’t have my hardware in yet), I will keep tweaking this for a little while to see if I can make it play as nicely as regular controller triggers do, if not better.
[/list]

The default release number for Touch is so much smaller because the spring on Touch controller triggers is much weaker than the Vive's trigger spring.

The release value is basically how far the trigger needs to move back up for your hand to release the thing it's holding.

(Knuckles controllers also respond to the release sensitivity, their default is 0.01)

notes.title: Update 4/18/2017
notes.content:
Upgrading to Unity 5.6 broke a bunch of things so I couldn’t push an update until they were fixed and I didn’t want to risk rolling back, sorry for the massive delay on everything!


Main game:
[list]
[*]Fixed external spectator camera freaking out.
[*]Added zoom screen for looking at people from far away. You get it by grabbing behind your neck!
[*]Made level list put unplayed levels at the start of the list.
[*]<Mixed Reality> Made the mixed reality camera not show the helmet/backpack as it sort of looked weird having it go through your body.
[*]<Mixed Reality> Made the mixed reality camera not show any of the comfort options as they were kind of weird and distracting.
[*]Upgraded game to Unity 5.6 in preparation of Linux support in the future.
[*]Added foot tracking for people with trackers, your feet will decide if you’re standing on something or not now instead of it just being an invisible line from your neck. Aside from that it shouldn’t change anything, feet are synched in multiplayer however.

[*]Upped menu button ignore delay after respawn to 2 seconds instead of 1.
[/list]

The game will also work with only 1 tracker, you can strap it to your body if you wish, just don’t hit calibrate feet if you don’t want to turn it into a foot. 

The game will use that tracker to decided if you’re standing on something instead of just checking from your neck down in the case of only 1 tracker.

notes.title: Skip levels in multiplayer! And some more Oculus Touch stuff.
notes.content:
Main game:
[list]
[*]Upgraded to the latest version of unity to hopefully make the game less crash prone.
[*]Added “Kalman filter” to Touch controllers to make them slightly nicer to play with, it smooths out any sudden jumps in tracking which happen when they’ve lost tracking and are being interpolated. In my tests it improved my jump consistency by a bit but if this has adverse effects for anyone else using Touch please let me know and I will tweak this further.
[*]Gave Touch users a tiny velocity boost when jumping to help with jump height.
[*]Fixed bug that made you sink into the floor slightly when walking while the floor is completely straight.
[*]Added Skip Level button only available to the host of a room that forces everyone in the server who hasn't finished yet to forfeit the level and goes to the next level in the playlist in multiplayer.
[*]Removed Head collide fade comfort option as it was causing some users to think their HMD was broken and generally went unused, it may be re-added later if requested, at which point I’ll try and make it so it’s not as buggy.
[/list]

The filter for Touch is mostly there because Touch seems to lose tracking around 10-11 meters per second of speed, you can check this yourself by seeing if you can get a higher speed number using a “SteamVR Advanced Settings” SteamVR add-on you can find on the web which has a statistics tab that keeps track of max controller speed.

notes.title: Small Trigger Sensitivity update!
notes.content:
Hey, not sure how many of you were following my video threads on reddit but I was having issues with Touch tracking when making jumps- this was slightly remedied by making sure I had no USB 2.0 sensors but jumping still didn't feel right so I started looking at how I'm doing the triggers.

This small update makes it so the triggers are way more sensitive, but still depend on the value your triggers can produce so even glitchy triggers that don't get the full 0-1 range should have this work fine.

Main game:
[list]
[*]Made trigger more sensitive- this makes jumping feel better for both Vive and Touch users, it's pretty great.
[*]Added small arrow pointing out the forward direction of your playspace if you have center of room turned on. This makes it much easier for Touch users to find their forward direction and makes it easier to keep things aligned with that direction by rotating the playspace.
[/list]

I do have to say that Touch users still have a slight disadvantage as of right now, it seems Oculus still has some minor glitches in their tracking to deal with, if these problems persist I'll look into assisting jumps for Touch users but it really only causes issues with very large jumps, which are generally avoided in most of the user created levels and all of the built in ones, unless the user tries skipping large chunks of levels.

notes.title: Colorcoding and playspace rotation!
notes.content:
Minor update while I work on getting the first proper gamemode in! Stay tuned, might be a few days.

[img]http://puu.sh/slki8/cd3f462cd0.gif[/img]

Main game:
[list]
[*]Made the workshop level list a colorcoded- Green is unplayed/new, blue is played(/completed). It also records your best time in both online and offline playthroughs.
[*]Added button to skybox interface next to color selection to open the skyboxes folder in your install folder.
[*]Added toggle for making the touchpad rotate you in 45 degree increments (90 on moving platforms for…technical reasons.), this makes it possible to play the game even if you can’t physically rotate your body for one reason or another. It’s not ideal and kind of breaks doing hand gestures and will likely not work for all levels that want you to turn but it’s a decent step for accessibility. It’s currently disabled in the level editor as that sort of breaks the spawn menu which is too essential, the free movement in the level editor should suffice to offset that anyway.
[*]Hitting the backslash key activates a mixed reality mode where the “externalcamera.cfg” numbers are based off of local rotation/position offset off one of the lighthouses, pressing “]” switches what lighthouse it bases its position off of. This feature is mostly useful for folks doing mixed reality without having a third controller, though it won’t be compatible with a third controller setup, just adding a 3rd controller for mixed reality should still work fine however.
[/list]

The mixed reality thing is really only interesting for folks into trying to do that, but it being based off of the lighthouse position/rotation makes it possible to set up without needing to hack a third controller into SteamVR, I’m hoping they’ll allow this natively at some point but until then my solution will work fine. :)

More stuff soon!
